lessons.title: Nutrition and its five steps

videos.title: Steps of nutrition in humans (parent to choose)

cards.title: What is a nutrient?
cards.body: "A nutrient is a component of food that provides nourishment to the body for its growth and maintenance."

cards.title: The five major nutrients
cards.body: Carbohydrates and fats provide energy. Proteins help our body to grow. Minerals and vitamins protect our body.
cards.example: Carbohydrates: rice, sugar, potato · Fats: oil, butter · Proteins: eggs, meat, pulses, cheese · Minerals: calcium, iodine, sodium · Vitamins: Vitamin D, Vitamin K
cards.reveal: Proteins act as building blocks of our body.

cards.title: What is nutrition?
cards.body: "The process by which organisms obtain and use food is known as nutrition."
cards.didYouKnow: Plants synthesize their food. Animals obtain theirs.

cards.title: Five steps: ingestion and digestion
cards.body: Ingestion: "The process by which food is taken in by the organisms." Digestion: "It is the process of breaking down of complex food into simpler absorbable molecules so that it get easily absorbed in our body."

cards.title: Five steps: absorption and assimilation
cards.body: Absorption: "It is the process by which digested food is taken up (absorbed) by the cells of our body." Assimilation: "The absorbed food is utilized by living cells and is used by the body for its growth and other purposes."

cards.title: Five steps: egestion
cards.body: Egestion: "It is the process by which undigested food is removed from the body."
cards.reveal: In order: ingestion → digestion → absorption → assimilation → egestion

practice.prompt: Which nutrients provide energy and warmth to our body?
practice.explanation: Fats provide energy and warmth to our body, e.g. oil and butter.
hints: Think of oil and butter.

practice.prompt: Put the five steps of nutrition in order.
practice.explanation: Food is taken in, broken down, taken up by cells, used by the body, and what is left is removed.
hints: Food is taken in first, and removed last.

practice.prompt: The process by which undigested food is removed from the body is called ____.
practice.explanation: Egestion: the process by which undigested food is removed from the body.
hints: It starts with "e".

practice.prompt: Which nutrients act as building blocks of our body?
practice.explanation: Proteins help our body to grow and act as building blocks of our body.
hints: Eggs, meat, pulses and cheese.

lessons.notebook: In your notebook, draw five boxes joined by arrows and write the five steps of nutrition in order. Under each box, write one line from your book about it.

check.prompt: A ____ is a component of food that provides nourishment to the body for its growth and maintenance.
check.explanation: This is the book’s definition of a nutrient (p.48).

check.prompt: Rice, sugar and potato are examples of
check.explanation: Carbohydrates provide energy, e.g. rice, sugar and potato.

check.prompt: Assimilation is the process by which food is taken in by the organisms.
check.explanation: That is ingestion. Assimilation is when the absorbed food is utilized by living cells.

check.prompt: Breaking down complex food into simpler absorbable molecules is called
check.explanation: Digestion is the process of breaking down of complex food into simpler absorbable molecules.

keyRules: A nutrient is a component of food that provides nourishment to the body for its growth and maintenance.
The process by which organisms obtain and use food is known as nutrition.
In the human body, the process of nutrition involves five steps: ingestion, digestion, absorption, assimilation and egestion.

lessons.title: The alimentary canal, mouth and teeth

videos.title: Human digestive system and types of teeth (parent to choose)

warmup.front: What are the five steps of nutrition?
warmup.back: Ingestion, digestion, absorption, assimilation and egestion.

cards.title: Two parts of the digestive system
cards.body: Our digestive system is formed of two parts: the alimentary canal and the digestive glands.
cards.reveal: Digestive glands: salivary glands, liver and pancreas

cards.title: The alimentary canal
cards.body: "Alimentary canal is a long, muscular and coiled tube. It starts from the mouth and ends at the anus."
cards.example: Mouth or buccal cavity → Oesophagus (gullet) → Stomach → Small Intestine → Large Intestine → Anus

cards.title: The digestive system
cards.body: "The alimentary canal along with the associated glands is called the digestive system (Fig. 4.1)."

cards.title: The mouth
cards.body: The mouth contains the tongue, teeth and salivary glands. Taking food into the mouth is called ingestion. Digestion starts in the mouth itself.
cards.reveal: Food is chewed (masticated) by the teeth.

cards.title: Four kinds of teeth
cards.body: Incisors (front four, flat) bite and cut. Canines (sharp, two) tear. Premolars and molars grind and crush.
cards.example: Table 4.1, number in each jaw: Incisors 4 · Canines 2 · Premolars 4 · Molars 6

cards.title: Milk teeth and permanent teeth
cards.body: The first set of teeth in a baby are called milk teeth. These are later replaced by permanent teeth (about 12–14 years of age).
cards.didYouKnow: At birth, a human infant has no teeth. Milk teeth are twenty in number. Each jaw in an adult has 16 teeth (32 teeth in all).

practice.prompt: Put the organs of the alimentary canal in order, from where food goes in.
practice.explanation: The alimentary canal starts from the mouth and ends at the anus (p.49).
hints: It starts at the mouth and ends at the anus.

practice.prompt: Match each type of tooth to its job.
practice.explanation: Table 4.1 (p.50).
hints: The sharp ones tear. The flat front ones bite.

practice.prompt: Each jaw in an adult has ____ teeth.
practice.explanation: Each jaw in an adult has 16 teeth (32 teeth in all).

practice.prompt: Which of these is a digestive gland?
practice.explanation: The digestive glands are the salivary glands, liver and pancreas.
hints: Three glands: salivary glands, liver, pancreas.

lessons.notebook: Investigation 4.1 (p.50): stand in front of a mirror and count your teeth. Draw the shape of a front tooth and a back tooth in your notebook, and write which kind each one is.

check.prompt: The alimentary canal starts from the mouth and ends at the ____.
check.explanation: Alimentary canal: a long, muscular and coiled tube from the mouth to the anus.

check.prompt: The front four teeth in each jaw are the
check.explanation: The front four teeth in each jaw are the incisors. They are flat and help in biting and cutting.

check.prompt: Canines are sharp and two in number in each jaw.
check.explanation: On either side of the incisors are the canines. These are sharp and two in number in each jaw.

check.prompt: The last molars that appear at the age of eighteen or even later are called
check.explanation: The last molars appear at the age of eighteen or even later. These are called the wisdom teeth.

check.prompt: The alimentary canal along with the associated glands is called the ____.
check.explanation: This is the book’s definition of the digestive system (p.49).

keyRules: Alimentary canal is a long, muscular and coiled tube. It starts from the mouth and ends at the anus.
The alimentary canal along with the associated glands is called the digestive system.
Incisors: biting & cutting · Canines: tearing food · Premolars and molars: grinding and crushing food.

lessons.title: Tongue, salivary glands, oesophagus and stomach

videos.title: Saliva, oesophagus and stomach (parent to choose)

warmup.front: Which teeth are meant for tearing the food?

cards.title: The tongue
cards.body: Tongue helps in mixing the chewed food with saliva and swallowing the food. It also helps us to taste the food and to speak.
cards.reveal: Taste buds distinguish four basic tastes – salt, sour, sweet and bitter (Fig. 4.3).

cards.title: Salivary glands and saliva
cards.body: There are three pairs of salivary glands in our mouth. They secrete a watery material called saliva.
cards.example: Saliva contains an enzyme called amylase (also called ptyalin) which acts on starch and break it into simple sugar.
cards.didYouKnow: Saliva also helps in killing the germs in mouth and in ingested food.

cards.title: The oesophagus
cards.body: Oesophagus connects the mouth cavity with the stomach. It is also called the food pipe and it has no role in digestion.
cards.reveal: It pushes the food mixed with saliva (bolus) into the stomach by peristalsis.

cards.title: Peristalsis
cards.body: "Peristalsis is the wave-like movement due to sequential (one after the other) contraction of muscles in the wall of the oesophagus. The movement enables the food to be pushed forward in the alimentary canal."

cards.title: The stomach
cards.body: The stomach is a muscular, J-shaped, bag-like structure in the upper abdomen. Here the food is churned and converted into a semi-solid paste.
cards.reveal: Food remains in the stomach for about 4–5 hours.

cards.title: Gastric juice and hydrochloric acid
cards.body: The stomach secretes gastric juice and hydrochloric acid. The acid kills the germs in the food and activates the gastric juice. Proteins are digested by the gastric juice partly in stomach.
cards.example: The partly digested food (chyme) then passes into the small intestine.
cards.didYouKnow: Milk has casein protein, digested by the enzyme rennin, found abundantly in the stomach of infants.

practice.prompt: Saliva contains an enzyme called amylase, also called
practice.explanation: Saliva contains an enzyme called amylase (also called ptyalin).
hints: It starts with "p" but it is not pepsin.

practice.prompt: The food mixed with saliva is called ____.
practice.explanation: The oesophagus pushes the food mixed with saliva (bolus) into the stomach.
hints: It is in brackets in your book on p.51.

practice.prompt: The oesophagus has no role in digestion.
practice.explanation: It is also called the food pipe and it has no role in digestion. It only pushes the bolus to the stomach.
hints: What does the book say the food pipe does?

practice.prompt: The partly digested food that passes from the stomach to the small intestine is called
practice.explanation: The partly digested food (chyme) then passes into the small intestine.
hints: Bolus goes INTO the stomach. What comes OUT?

lessons.notebook: Chew a small piece of bread slowly for a few minutes (ask a grown-up first). In your notebook, write how the taste changed and which part of saliva does this (p.50).

check.prompt: There are three pairs of ____ glands in our mouth.
check.explanation: There are three pairs of salivary glands in our mouth (p.50).

check.prompt: Taste buds on the tongue distinguish four basic tastes. Which is NOT one of them?
check.explanation: The four basic tastes are salt, sour, sweet and bitter (Fig. 4.3).

check.prompt: The stomach is a muscular, ____-shaped, bag-like structure.
check.explanation: The stomach is a muscular, J-shaped, bag-like structure in the upper abdomen.

check.prompt: The hydrochloric acid in the stomach kills the germs which may be present in the food.
check.explanation: The acid kills the germs and also activates the gastric juice.

check.prompt: Food remains in the stomach for about
check.explanation: Here, food remains for about 4–5 hours (p.51).

keyRules: Saliva contains an enzyme called amylase (also called ptyalin) which acts on starch and break it into simple sugar.
Peristalsis is the wave-like movement due to sequential (one after the other) contraction of muscles in the wall of the oesophagus.
The stomach secretes a juice called gastric juice and hydrochloric acid.

lessons.title: Small intestine, large intestine, liver and pancreas

videos.title: Small intestine, villi and large intestine (parent to choose)

warmup.front: What is the partly digested food that leaves the stomach called?

cards.title: The small intestine
cards.body: Small intestine is a long coiled tube. It secretes intestinal juice which helps in the digestion of all types of food.
cards.reveal: Food is converted into simple form like glucose, amino acids and fatty acids, etc.

cards.title: Villi
cards.body: The inner surface of the small intestine has a number of finger-like projections called villi (Fig. 4.4). They absorb the end products of digestion.
cards.didYouKnow: The villi contain microvilli, which increase the area for absorption.

cards.title: Where the food goes next
cards.body: Sugar and amino acids pass into the blood system. Fats pass into lymph vessels (lacteals). Vitamins and minerals get directly absorbed in the intestinal walls.

cards.title: The large intestine
cards.body: This part does not play any role in the digestion of food. It helps in absorbing water from the undigested food.
cards.reveal: The semi-solid undigested food (faeces) passes into the last part, called rectum.

cards.title: Rectum, anus and egestion
cards.body: "The rectum opens into anus through which faeces are expelled out of the body. This process of eliminating undigested food through anus is called egestion."

cards.title: Liver and pancreas
cards.body: The liver is the largest gland in human body. It secretes bile juice, stored in the gall bladder. Bile helps in the digestion of fats.
cards.example: The pancreas secretes insulin, which helps to maintain normal sugar level in the blood (Fig. 4.5).

practice.prompt: The finger-like projections in the small intestine are called ____.
practice.explanation: The inner surface of the small intestine has a number of finger-like projections called villi.

practice.prompt: The absorbed fats pass into
practice.explanation: The absorbed fats passes into lymph vessels (lacteals). Sugar and amino acids pass into the blood.
hints: Look for the word in brackets on p.51.

practice.prompt: Bile juice is stored in a small bag called the
practice.explanation: The liver secretes bile juice which is stored in a small bag called the gall bladder.

practice.prompt: The large intestine helps in absorbing water from the undigested food.
practice.explanation: It plays no role in digestion, but it absorbs water from the undigested food.
hints: What does the large intestine take out of the undigested food?

lessons.notebook: Copy Fig. 4.4 (p.51) into your notebook: small intestine → a fold of the lining → a villus (label lacteal and capillary) → epithelial cell.

check.prompt: The largest gland in the human body is the
check.explanation: The liver is the largest gland in human body (p.52).

check.prompt: Which organ secretes insulin?
check.explanation: The pancreas secretes insulin, which helps to maintain normal sugar level in the blood.

check.prompt: The last part of the large intestine is called the ____.
check.explanation: The faeces pass into the last part of large intestine called rectum.

check.prompt: The large intestine plays a big role in the digestion of food.
check.explanation: The large intestine does not play any role in the digestion of food. It absorbs water.

check.prompt: Bile helps in the digestion of
check.explanation: Bile helps in the digestion of fats (p.52).

keyRules: Small intestine is a long coiled tube. It secretes intestinal juice which helps in the digestion of all types of food.
The large intestine does not play any role in the digestion of food. It helps in absorbing water from the undigested food.
This process of eliminating undigested food through anus is called egestion.
The liver is the largest gland in human body. It secretes bile juice which is stored in a small bag called the gall bladder.

lessons.title: Digestion in humans: enzymes

videos.title: Digestive enzymes and the iodine starch test (parent to choose)

cards.title: Enzymes
cards.body: "Enzymes are proteins in nature. These act as catalysts." The process of digestion is brought about with the help of digestive juices containing enzymes.

cards.title: Mouth and stomach
cards.body: Mouth: saliva (amylase) acts on starch (a carbohydrate) → sugars. Stomach: gastric juice (pepsin) acts on proteins → peptides.

cards.title: The pancreas: three enzymes
cards.body: Pancreatic amylase: starch → maltose. Trypsin: proteins → peptides. Lipase: fats → fatty acids.

cards.title: The small intestine
cards.body: Intestinal juice (several enzymes) acts on partially digested proteins and carbohydrates (received from stomach) → simple sugars, amino acids, etc.

cards.title: Investigation 4.2: the iodine test
cards.body: Tube A: potato pieces + water. Tube B: potato pieces + water + amylase. After 30 minutes, add iodine solution to both.
cards.reveal: A turns blue-black (starch is there). B does not change in colour: the amylase digested the starch.

practice.prompt: Match each enzyme to the food it acts on.
practice.explanation: Table 4.2 (p.52).
hints: Lipase sounds a bit like "lipid", another word for fat… but check Table 4.2.

practice.prompt: Lipase acts on fats and forms ____.
practice.explanation: Lipase: fats → fatty acids (Table 4.2).
hints: Fats → fatty ____.

practice.prompt: In Investigation 4.2, which test tube turns blue-black with iodine?
practice.explanation: Iodine turns starch blue-black. In B the amylase digested the starch, so B did not change colour.
hints: Which tube still has its starch?

lessons.notebook: Copy Table 4.2 (p.52) into your notebook with four columns: part, enzyme/juice, target nutrient, product formed.

check.prompt: Enzymes are proteins in nature and act as catalysts.
check.explanation: Key ideas, p.48.

check.prompt: Pancreatic amylase acts on starch and forms
check.explanation: Pancreatic amylase: starch → maltose (Table 4.2).

check.prompt: Trypsin acts on
check.explanation: Trypsin: proteins → peptides (Table 4.2).

check.prompt: Iodine solution turns starch ____.
check.explanation: When iodine reacts with starch, the potato pieces turn blue-black (Investigation 4.2).

keyRules: Enzymes are proteins in nature. These act as catalysts.
The process of digestion is brought about with the help of digestive juices containing enzymes.

lessons.title: Indigestion and healthy food habits

videos.title: Healthy food habits for kids (parent to choose)

warmup.front: Which enzyme from the pancreas acts on fats?

cards.title: What is indigestion?
cards.body: "Indigestion (also known as dyspepsia) is the condition of impaired digestion. It results in persistent discomfort and pain in the stomach."

cards.title: Signs of indigestion
cards.body: Stomach pain, vomiting, excessive gas formation, bloating of stomach and a burning sensation in the stomach.
cards.reveal: Symptoms of indigestion must not be ignored — see your doctor right away.

cards.title: What causes it?
cards.body: Overeating or eating too fast, lying down soon after meals, drinking too much alcohol, eating spicy, oily and fatty foods, and smoking.

cards.title: Healthy food habits (1)
cards.body: Eat a balanced diet, keeping in mind your age, health and occupation. Eat clean food, protected from dust, houseflies and mosquitoes. Eat properly cooked fresh food.

cards.title: Healthy food habits (2)
cards.body: Avoid fried foods. Use clean utensils. Take green salad, green vegetables and fruits. Drink large quantity of clean filtered water. Chew food well. Develop regular eating habits.

practice.prompt: Indigestion is also known as ____.
practice.explanation: Indigestion (also known as dyspepsia) is the condition of impaired digestion.
hints: It is in brackets on p.53.

practice.prompt: Which of these is a healthy food habit?
practice.explanation: Chewing food well is a healthy habit. Lying down soon after meals and eating too fast cause indigestion.
hints: Two of these are causes of indigestion.

practice.prompt: Eating spicy, oily and fatty foods can cause indigestion.
practice.explanation: It is one of the causes of indigestion listed on p.53.
hints: Look at "Causes of indigestion".

lessons.notebook: Make a "My healthy food habits" chart in your notebook with the habits from p.53. Tick the ones you already follow this week.

check.prompt: Which is a symptom of indigestion?
check.explanation: Bloating of stomach is listed among the common symptoms (p.53).

check.prompt: Which is a cause of indigestion?
check.explanation: Overeating or eating too fast is a cause of indigestion.

check.prompt: Food should be kept protected from dust, houseflies and mosquitoes.
check.explanation: Eat clean food which is kept protected from dust, houseflies and mosquitoes.

keyRules: Indigestion (also known as dyspepsia) is the condition of impaired digestion. It results in persistent discomfort and pain in the stomach.
For maintaining good health, we need to develop and maintain good food habits.

questionBank.prompt: Which of the following is not a step of nutrition in humans?
questionBank.explanation: The five steps are ingestion, digestion, absorption, assimilation and egestion. Reabsorption is not one of them.

questionBank.prompt: Define: Ingestion
questionBank.modelAnswer: Ingestion is the process by which food is taken in by the organisms.
questionBank.explanation: From the five steps of nutrition (p.49).

questionBank.prompt: Define: Absorption
questionBank.modelAnswer: Absorption is the process by which digested food is taken up (absorbed) by the cells of our body.
questionBank.explanation: From the five steps of nutrition (p.49).

questionBank.prompt: Define: Digestion
questionBank.modelAnswer: Digestion is the process of breaking down of complex food into simpler absorbable molecules so that it get easily absorbed in our body.
questionBank.explanation: From the five steps of nutrition (p.49).

questionBank.prompt: Define: Assimilation
questionBank.modelAnswer: Assimilation: the absorbed food is utilized by living cells and is used by the body for its growth and other purposes.
questionBank.explanation: From the five steps of nutrition (p.49).

questionBank.prompt: Mention various steps take place in the process of digestion in human.
questionBank.modelAnswer: Ingestion (food is taken in), digestion (complex food is broken down into simpler absorbable molecules), absorption (digested food is taken up by the cells), assimilation (absorbed food is used by the cells for growth) and egestion (undigested food is removed from the body).
questionBank.explanation: These are the five steps of nutrition in the human body (p.49).

questionBank.prompt: What is the process of utilisation of food material by the body?
questionBank.explanation: Assimilation: the absorbed food is utilized by living cells and is used by the body for its growth and other purposes.

questionBank.prompt: Define: Digestive system

questionBank.prompt: Describe the functions of the tongue.
questionBank.modelAnswer: The tongue helps in mixing the chewed food with saliva and swallowing the food. It helps us to taste the food, as it has taste buds which distinguish salt, sour, sweet and bitter. It also helps us to speak.
questionBank.explanation: From "Tongue" on p.50.

questionBank.prompt: Name the secretions of stomach.

questionBank.prompt: A piece of bread was placed in the mouth for a few minutes. Students observed the changes in taste and named the enzyme involved. Which is right?

questionBank.prompt: Define: Enzymes

questionBank.prompt: Name the digestive juices secreted by mouth, pancreas, stomach and small intestine.
questionBank.modelAnswer: Mouth: saliva (amylase). Pancreas: pancreatic amylase, trypsin and lipase. Stomach: gastric juice (pepsin). Small intestine: intestinal juice (several enzymes).

questionBank.prompt: Protein: give the name of the digestive juice/enzyme and the product formed.

questionBank.prompt: Starch: give the name of the digestive juice/enzyme and the product formed.

questionBank.prompt: Give a brief of enzymes found in the digestive juices secreted by different parts of digestive system.
questionBank.modelAnswer: Mouth — saliva (amylase): starch → sugars. Stomach — gastric juice (pepsin): proteins → peptides. Pancreas — pancreatic amylase: starch → maltose; trypsin: proteins → peptides; lipase: fats → fatty acids. Small intestine — intestinal juice (several enzymes): partially digested proteins and carbohydrates → simple sugars, amino acids, etc.

questionBank.prompt: Which enzyme helps in the digestion of fats, and which organ secretes it?

questionBank.prompt: What is indigestion?
questionBank.modelAnswer: Indigestion (also known as dyspepsia) is the condition of impaired digestion. It results in persistent discomfort and pain in the stomach.

questionBank.prompt: Write any three common symptoms of indigestion.
questionBank.modelAnswer: Any three of: stomach pain, vomiting, excessive gas formation, bloating of stomach, burning sensation in the stomach.

questionBank.prompt: Write any three causes of indigestion.

questionBank.prompt: Write five healthy food habits.

questionBank.prompt: If symptoms of indigestion do not go away, what should you do?
